en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn to say how people do things, like drive carefully or speak English well, and how to make words stronger or softer. Let's take it one small step at a time.

steps.title: How? Add -ly
steps.text: You know adjectives like slow and careful. Now let's say how someone does something.
steps.body:
An **adjective** describes a person or thing: *a slow bus*. An **adverb** describes **how** someone does something: The bus moves **slowly**. Most adverbs are **adjective + -ly**. Indonesian keeps the same word (*pelan*, sometimes *dengan pelan*), but English changes it.

Spelling: careful → carefu**ll**y (two l's). Consonant + **y** → **-ily**: easy → easily. **-le** → **-ly**: gentle → gently.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Let's try the spelling. The adjective is happy.

question.prompt: Complete: The children are playing ___ in the park.
question.explanation: happy ends in a consonant + **y**, so y changes to **i** before -ly: **happily**. *happy* alone is the adjective: it can't say how they play.

steps.title: No -ly: fast, hard, well
steps.text: A few adverbs break the -ly rule. Just remember them.
steps.body: **fast, hard, early, late** don't change: a fast train → it goes **fast**. **good → well**. No 'fastly', no 'goodly'. Careful: **hardly** is a different word = *hampir tidak*. *He works hard* = he works a lot; *He hardly works* = he almost doesn't work!

examples.en: The train to Bandung goes very fast.
examples.id: Kereta ke Bandung melaju sangat cepat.

examples.en: Pak Hasan works hard every day.
examples.id: Pak Hasan bekerja keras setiap hari.

examples.en: I sometimes get up late on Sundays.
examples.id: Kadang saya bangun siang di hari Minggu.

examples.en: Bu Ani cooks rendang really well.
examples.id: Bu Ani jago sekali memasak rendang.

examples.en: He hardly sleeps. He's very busy.
examples.id: Dia hampir tidak tidur. Dia sangat sibuk.

steps.title: Adjective or adverb?
steps.text: Here's the Indonesian trap. Ask one question: a person or thing, or how?
steps.body:
A person or thing → **adjective**: *a careful driver*. After **am/is/are** too: *Budi is careful*. How someone does something → **adverb**: *Budi drives carefully*. Indonesian says *hati-hati* for both. Trick: if Indonesian can say *dengan ...*, English needs the adverb.

**friendly** ends in -ly but is an adjective (*a friendly waiter*). And I'm **well** is right: there well means **healthy** (*sehat*).

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Budi plays football every Sunday. How does he play?

question.prompt: Budi is a good footballer. Complete: He plays very ___.
question.explanation: This says **how** he plays, so it needs the adverb, and the adverb of good is **well**: very **well**. *good* describes a person or thing (*a good footballer*), and 'goodly' doesn't exist.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Now the other way round: is this about a person, or about how?

question.prompt: Sari never makes mistakes. Complete: She's a ___ worker.
question.explanation: The word describes a person (a ___ **worker**), so use the **adjective**: a **careful** worker. *carefully* says how someone does something, and 'carefuly' is a spelling mistake.

steps.title: Where does the adverb go?
steps.text: Last thing about adverbs: where to put them.
steps.body: Put the adverb **after the verb**, or after the verb + its **object** (the thing after the verb, like *Mandarin* in *speaks Mandarin*). Never between them: not `speaks fluently Mandarin`. Indonesian has the same order: *berbicara bahasa Mandarin dengan lancar*.

examples.en: Dimas speaks Mandarin fluently.
examples.id: Dimas berbicara bahasa Mandarin dengan lancar.

examples.en: Please read the contract carefully.
examples.id: Tolong baca kontraknya dengan teliti.

examples.en: My son writes his name very neatly.
examples.id: Anak laki-laki saya menulis namanya dengan sangat rapi.

examples.en: Can you explain it slowly, please?
examples.id: Bisakah kamu menjelaskannya pelan-pelan?

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Rina has piano lessons every week. Say she plays it well.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Rina bermain piano dengan baik.
question.explanation: First the verb and its object (**plays the piano**), then the adverb **well** at the end. 'Rina plays well the piano' puts the adverb between the verb and the object.

steps.title: very, really, quite
steps.text: Now let's make words stronger or softer.
steps.body: **very** and **really** make a word stronger; **quite** makes it a little softer (= *cukup, lumayan*). They go **right before** an adjective or adverb: *very slowly, quite well*. Before a **verb**, only **really**: *I really like it*, not `I very like it`. Indonesian *sangat suka* tempts you to say 'very like'. In American English, quite is often as strong as very.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Dimas watches every football match on TV. Which sentence is right?

question.explanation: likes is a verb, and only **really** can go before a verb: Dimas **really likes** football. *very* only goes before an adjective or adverb (very good, very well).

steps.text: Here is the whole lesson on one page.

a friendly waiter (in a friendly way)
Dimas berbicara bahasa Mandarin dengan lancar.
very / really / quite + adjective or adverb

sangat pelan, sangat bagus, cukup baik
tips: If Indonesian can say **dengan ...** (dengan hati-hati), English needs the adverb.
After **am / is / are**, use the adjective: She is **careful**, not `She is carefully`.
Not `I very like it`: before a verb, use **really**.

id.greeting: Halo! Hari ini kamu akan belajar menjelaskan bagaimana orang melakukan sesuatu, misalnya menyetir dengan hati-hati atau berbicara bahasa Inggris dengan baik, dan cara menguatkan atau melemahkan kata. Kita pelajari pelan-pelan, satu langkah kecil setiap kali.

steps.title: Bagaimana? Tambah -ly
steps.text: Kamu sudah kenal kata sifat seperti slow dan careful. Sekarang yuk jelaskan bagaimana seseorang melakukan sesuatu.
steps.body:
**Kata sifat** (adjective) menjelaskan orang atau benda: *a slow bus* (bus yang lambat). **Adverb** (kata keterangan cara) menjelaskan **bagaimana** seseorang melakukan sesuatu: The bus moves **slowly** (busnya bergerak pelan). Kebanyakan adverb = **kata sifat + -ly**. Bahasa Indonesia memakai kata yang sama (*pelan*, kadang *dengan pelan*), tapi bahasa Inggris mengubahnya.

Ejaan: careful → carefu**ll**y (dua l). Konsonan + **y** → **-ily**: easy → easily. **-le** → **-ly**: gentle → gently.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Yuk coba ejaannya. Kata sifatnya happy.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: The children are playing ___ in the park.
question.explanation: happy berakhir dengan konsonan + **y**, jadi y berubah menjadi **i** sebelum -ly: **happily**. *happy* saja adalah kata sifat: tidak bisa menjelaskan cara mereka bermain.

steps.title: Tanpa -ly: fast, hard, well
steps.text: Ada beberapa adverb yang tidak ikut aturan -ly. Cukup dihafal saja.
steps.body: **fast, hard, early, late** tidak berubah: a fast train → it goes **fast**. **good → well**. Tidak ada 'fastly' atau 'goodly'. Hati-hati: **hardly** adalah kata lain = *hampir tidak*. *He works hard* = dia bekerja keras; *He hardly works* = dia hampir tidak bekerja!

examples.id: Kereta ke Bandung melaju sangat cepat.

examples.id: Pak Hasan bekerja keras setiap hari.

examples.en: I sometimes get up late on Sundays.
examples.id: Kadang saya bangun siang di hari Minggu.

examples.en: Bu Ani cooks rendang really well.
examples.id: Bu Ani jago sekali memasak rendang.

examples.en: He hardly sleeps. He's very busy.
examples.id: Dia hampir tidak tidur. Dia sangat sibuk.

steps.title: Kata sifat atau adverb?
steps.text: Ini jebakan bahasa Indonesia. Tanyakan satu hal: orang atau benda, atau caranya?
steps.body:
Orang atau benda → **kata sifat**: *a careful driver*. Setelah **am/is/are** juga: *Budi is careful*. Cara seseorang melakukan sesuatu → **adverb**: *Budi drives carefully*. Bahasa Indonesia bilang *hati-hati* untuk keduanya. Triknya: kalau bahasa Indonesia bisa pakai *dengan ...*, bahasa Inggris butuh adverb.

**friendly** berakhir -ly tapi kata sifat (*a friendly waiter*). Dan I'm **well** itu benar: di sini well artinya **sehat**.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Budi main sepak bola setiap hari Minggu. Bagaimana cara dia bermain?

question.prompt: Budi pemain sepak bola yang bagus. Lengkapi: He plays very ___.
question.explanation: Kalimat ini menjelaskan **cara** dia bermain, jadi butuh adverb, dan adverb dari good adalah **well**: very **well**. *good* menjelaskan orang atau benda (*a good footballer*), dan kata 'goodly' tidak ada.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Sekarang sebaliknya: ini tentang orang, atau tentang caranya?

question.prompt: Sari tidak pernah membuat kesalahan. Lengkapi: She's a ___ worker.
question.explanation: Katanya menjelaskan orang (a ___ **worker**), jadi pakai **kata sifat**: a **careful** worker. *carefully* menjelaskan cara melakukan sesuatu, dan 'carefuly' salah eja.

steps.title: Di mana letak adverb?
steps.text: Hal terakhir tentang adverb: di mana menaruhnya.
steps.body: Taruh adverb **setelah kata kerja**, atau setelah kata kerja + **objeknya** (benda setelah kata kerja, misalnya *Mandarin* di *speaks Mandarin*). Jangan di antara keduanya: bukan `speaks fluently Mandarin`. Urutan bahasa Indonesia sama: *berbicara bahasa Mandarin dengan lancar*.

examples.en: Dimas speaks Mandarin fluently.
examples.id: Dimas berbicara bahasa Mandarin dengan lancar.

steps.title: Susun kalimat
steps.text: Rina les piano setiap minggu. Bilang bahwa dia bermain dengan baik.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Rina bermain piano dengan baik.
question.explanation: Pertama kata kerja dan objeknya (**plays the piano**), lalu adverb **well** di akhir. 'Rina plays well the piano' menaruh adverb di antara kata kerja dan objek.

steps.title: very, really, quite
steps.text: Sekarang yuk buat kata lebih kuat atau lebih lemah.
steps.body: **very** dan **really** membuat kata lebih kuat; **quite** membuatnya sedikit lebih lemah (= *cukup, lumayan*). Letaknya **tepat sebelum** kata sifat atau adverb: *very slowly, quite well*. Sebelum **kata kerja**, hanya **really**: *I really like it*, bukan `I very like it`. *Sangat suka* membuat orang tergoda bilang 'very like'. Dalam bahasa Inggris Amerika, quite sering sama kuatnya dengan very.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Dimas menonton setiap pertandingan sepak bola di TV. Kalimat mana yang benar?

question.explanation: likes adalah kata kerja, dan hanya **really** yang bisa ada sebelum kata kerja: Dimas **really likes** football. *very* hanya ada sebelum kata sifat atau adverb (very good, very well).
